chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from some of his companions, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Haydara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Jihad is the most superior of things after the obligatory duties.

key_terms.الْجِهَادُ: Jihad: literally 'striving' or 'exertion'; encompasses armed struggle in defense of the faith and community, as well as spiritual struggle against one's lower self
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضِ: al-fara'id (obligatory duties): the religious obligations incumbent upon every Muslim, including the five pillars — salat, sawm, zakat, hajj, and the testimony of faith

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the status of jihad among deeds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that jihad — striving in the way of God — ranks as the highest act of worship after fulfilling the obligatory religious duties (fara'id). This teaching underscores the supreme importance of jihad in the Islamic hierarchy of deeds, placing it above voluntary acts of worship, charity, and other supererogatory practices. In the Shia scholarly tradition, jihad encompasses both armed struggle in defense of the community and the broader spiritual striving against the self (jihad al-nafs).
